Lesson 4.2 · 16 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Sanction, the agreement packet and eSign

After this lesson you can:
  • Distinguish sanction from disbursement and explain sanction validity
  • Describe the execution packet and its integrity evidence
  • Explain conditions precedent vs conditions subsequent
On this page
  1. Sanction is an offer with an expiry date
  2. The execution packet
  3. Cooling-off: the borrower's exit door
  4. Where this lives in LoanOS
  5. Knowledge check

1. Sanction is an offer with an expiry date

The sanction letter records the approved amount, rate, tenor, charges, and — critically — conditions and a validity window. It is the RE's formal offer; the borrower's acceptance and the executed agreement turn it into a contract. Sanction validity is a real control: approvals go stale as circumstances change, so disbursement after expiry fails closed and forces reassessment.

Conditions come in two flavours a BA must never confuse:

  • Conditions precedent (CP) — must be satisfied or formally waived before money moves (e.g. insurance assignment, employer verification). An open CP blocks disbursement.
  • Conditions subsequent (CS) — obligations after disbursement (e.g. submit final property papers within 60 days), tracked with follow-up workflows.

2. The execution packet

Contracting produces a governed document set: KFS, sanction letter, agreement summary, privacy notice — rendered with checksums, delivered with evidence, signed with eSign (signer authentication, envelope, callback evidence) and vaulted with a receipt. Multi-party cases (co-borrowers, guarantors) require every party's signature to complete.

Each artefact carries integrity material: what was rendered, delivered, signed, by whom, when. Waivers of documents or conditions are themselves governed acts — policy reference, reason and a separate approver, per the origination journey design.

3. Cooling-off: the borrower's exit door

Digital lending's cooling-off period — a board-approved window after disbursement — lets the borrower exit by repaying principal plus proportionate APR-based cost, without penalty beyond that. The KFS disclosed it; servicing must honour it with a proper cancellation and refund workflow. It is a conduct control, not a courtesy.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DL-2025 — Cooling-off exit right and digital execution conduct.
  • RBI-KFS-2024 — KFS acceptance precedes execution; the packet embeds the disclosed terms.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability OFR-009 — Sanction letter with conditions and validity.
  • Capability DOC-011 — eSign envelope, signer authentication, callback and evidence.
  • Capability OFR-014 — Cooling-off cancellation, proportionate cost and refund.
  • Document docs/architecture/origination-journey.md — Governed journey: document verification/waiver, CP/CS evidence, sanction-validity fail-closed rule.

Key terms

Knowledge check

1. A sanction expired yesterday; the borrower's file is otherwise complete. Operations asks to disburse 'since it's only a day'. The platform's answer?

  1. Disburse with a note
  2. Disburse with manager sign-off
  3. Fail closed: expired sanction blocks disbursement until reassessment
  4. Extend validity retroactively
Show answer

C. Sanction validity is a control against stale approvals; the origination design makes post-expiry disbursement fail closed.

2. An open condition precedent exists but the borrower is pressing for funds. What can operations lawfully do?

  1. Disburse and chase the CP later
  2. Satisfy the CP with evidence, or obtain a governed waiver with policy reference, reason and a separate approver
  3. Convert it to a condition subsequent informally
  4. Delete the condition
Show answer

B. CPs block funds by definition; the only paths are evidenced satisfaction or a governed, independently approved waiver.
